subject: SSO session swapping during supplier invite flow — intermittent login failures
messages:
From: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@crownlogistics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Crown Logistics IT <it-support@crownlogistics.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Supplier portal invite — login swaps to other org session intermittently

Hi Irene,

We received the supplier invite link for our finance contact (Marla Jensen) and when she clicks the Coupa activation link she sometimes lands in an already-authenticated session for a different company in our browser. It looks like session cookies are being associated with the wrong tenant. She tried in Chrome (personal) and Edge (company) with the same result.

Steps we saw:
- Click invite link -> redirect to redwood auth -> SSO to IdP (Okta) -> redirect back to supplier portal -> ends up on another org profile
- When we open the link in incognito it works as expected

This is blocking PO acceptance for two suppliers this week. I attached a brief HAR and a screenshot showing the cookie headers. Can your team triage?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Procurement Ops
Crown Logistics

Attachments: screenshot_cookie_headers.png (image/png), sso_trace_20270403.txt (text/plain)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@crownlogistics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier portal invite — login swaps to other org session intermittently

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear repro and the attachments.

Quick triage: this looks like a session-binding edge case where a stale session cookie for a different tenant is being considered valid during the final redirect after SSO. The fact that incognito works points to a cookie scope / partitioning issue rather than IdP configuration.

What we'll do next:
- Ben, can you grab the trace and check our session binding logs around the relayState and tenant claim mapping? Check cookie domain/path and SameSite attributes.
- Alex, if you can, ask Marla to try the invite in a browser with all other accounts signed out and confirm whether clearing cookies for our domain fixes it — helps confirm browser-level cookie collision.
- I'll open a Jira ticket and propose a short-term mitigation: if relayState tenant claim is missing or ambiguous, present a tenant-chooser page before finalizing the session. That should avoid silently tying to an existing session.

I'll update once we have the logs.

Best,
Irene
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@crownlogistics.com>, Crown Logistics IT <it-support@crownlogistics.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier portal invite — login swaps to other org session intermittently

Folks — dug into the attached sso_trace_20270403.txt and our gateway logs. Notes below: 

- At t=2027-04-03T16:09:12Z we see the incoming SAML response with RelayState=rs-73c. RelayState does include tenant_id=crown-449 but the subsequent redirect response sets a session cookie with domain=.supplier.redwood.com and no explicit Partitioning header.
- Browser saw an existing session cookie for domain=.supplier.redwood.com from another tenant (tenant_id=orchid-112). Because we currently prefer existing session over relayState when a cookie is present, the tenant mapping short-circuits and the user lands in the wrong org.

Short-term mitigation options (ranked):
1) Server-side: When relayState includes tenant_id, always prefer relayState over an existing same-domain session cookie during the redirect flow. Low-risk change, quick rollout to prod via a config flag.
2) Client-side: Add a tenant-chooser splash page whenever a session cookie exists but relayState is present. UX mild friction.
3) Long-term: Move to cookie partitioning by top-level site (requires browser-compatible approach and careful rollout).

I can implement option (1) and push a canary to the staging cluster today for verification. Will add logs to Jira PROC-4521 and include a small test harness for the cookie collision case.

Ben
Senior Software Engineer, Platform

Attachments referenced: full gateway log excerpt (attached to Jira).
From: Alex Navarro <alex.navarro@crownlogistics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Crown Logistics IT <it-support@crownlogistics.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier portal invite — login swaps to other org session intermittently

Thanks — that plan sounds good and option (1) would be ideal for us. We can confirm quickly when you push the staging canary. Our IT team will stand by to retest with Marla when you have a candidate.

One quick ask: can you add a short rollback plan in case the change affects users who intentionally reuse accounts across tenants? We occasionally have procurement employees who manage multiple vendor orgs and we don’t want to force re-login in those cases.

Appreciate the fast response.

— Alex
Head of Procurement Ops, Crown Logistics
